nyana:study:1.title: Nyana rooiwalensis : South Africa's earliest near-complete sauropodomorph dinosaur skull from the Late Triassic of the Eastern Cape Province (Royal Society Open Science, 2026)

nyana:abstract:1.title: Nyana rooiwalensis : South Africa's earliest near-complete sauropodomorph dinosaur skull from the Late Triassic of the Eastern Cape Province (abstract)

facts.statement: Nyana is classified as a massopodan sauropodomorph dinosaur.
Nyana rooiwalensis lived during the Late Triassic Norian–Rhaetian ages in the Elliot Formation of South Africa.
facts.quote: Late Triassic (Norian–Rhaetian ages) Elliot Formation of South Africa

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Nyana rooiwalensis is a partial articulated skull and fragmentary skeleton of a juvenile that was three years old when it died.
facts.quote: known from a partial articulated skull and associated fragmentary skeleton of a juvenile individual, which was 3 years old when it died.

facts.statement: The fossil material of Nyana was discovered in 2018 in the lower Elliot Formation outcrops of Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
facts.quote: The Nyana fossil material was discovered in 2018 in outcrops of the lower Elliot Formation in Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Nyana rooiwalensis is catalogued as BP/1/8468 and is housed at the Evolutionary Studies Institute.
facts.quote: specimen BP/1/8468. It consists of a partial skeleton of a juvenile individual

facts.statement: The generic name Nyana means "son" or "child" in Xhosa and "small" in Sesotho.
facts.quote: The generic name, Nyana, is a word meaning son or child in Xhosa, as well as small in Sesotho.

facts.statement: The specific epithet rooiwalensis refers to the locality Rooiwal where the specimen was found.
facts.quote: The specific name, rooiwalensis, references the discovery of the only known specimen in Rooiwal.

facts.statement: Nyana belongs to the parent group Sauropodomorpha within the class Saurischia.
Nyana is known from a single fossil occurrence recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
The holotype skull of Nyana includes the braincase, palate, hyoid apparatus and scleral rings, making it the first near‑complete sauropodomorph skull from the lower Elliot Formation.
Body‑mass estimates suggest Nyana weighed about 400 kilograms.
